decisive_items: Hematoxylin-eosin staining demonstrated concentric proliferation of ovoid tumor cells
Smooth muscle actin (SMA) was diffusely positive in the tumor cells
CD31 immunostain highlighted many endothelial-lined vascular channels
response.rationale: Concentric perivascular ovoid cells with SMA-positive tumor cells and CD31 highlighting vessels, plus negative mature smooth muscle/melanocytic/STAT6/KSHV markers, best fits a glomus/perivascular tumor; other candidates are excluded by endothelial, squamous, or mesenchymal phenotypes.

rejected.why: H&E shows cellular ovoid tumor proliferation with mitoses/necrosis, not a simple vascular channel lesion; SMA-positive tumor cells are not endothelial.
History of SCC is incidental; histology lacks squamous differentiation and tumor cells are SMA positive, not epithelial.
No storiform spindle/fibrohistiocytic pattern; concentric perivascular ovoid cells and SMA-positive tumor cells are not typical.
Too nonspecific; CD31 only highlights vessels, while SMA-positive perivascular tumor cells point to a specific glomus tumor.
Tumor cells are SMA positive and CD31 only highlights vessels, not tumor cells; angiosarcoma would show CD31-positive endothelial tumor cells.
Clinical papule mimics BCC, but histology lacks basaloid nests/palisading and tumor cells are SMA positive.
DFSP is CD34-positive spindle cell tumor, not SMA-positive perivascular ovoid cells; no storiform pattern.
KSHV negative and histology is perivascular ovoid cells, not Kaposi spindle cells.
